user.name: User
user.short_desc: Your name, age, and a one-line description.

ai.name: Companion
ai.core_traits: Write your companion's personality traits here.
ai.persona_note: Write your companion's persona background here.

rhythm._comment: Minutes of user inactivity before deep memory integration runs. Default 60.
rhythm._comment_min_free: Skip the deep cycle when free RAM is below this many MB. Default 1200; lower it on small machines (e.g. 600), raise it if the host is shared.

context._comment: Total token budget for injected memory blocks (relevant_memories + memory_context + entity_context). Estimated as chars/4. Whole memories are dropped from the tail of the ranking, never cut mid-memory. Default 1200.

persona._comment: Persona layers (core / relationship / situational) and drift detection. Every key is optional; invalid values fall back to the defaults shown.
persona._comment_auto_apply: true = relationship-layer proposals are applied automatically (at most weekly_apply_limit per 7 days); false = every proposal waits as 'pending' for manual review via /api/persona/proposals.
persona._comment_drift_check: Daily drift check: fixed probe questions are answered with the full persona and compared with anchor answers stored when the core prompt version was created. Below the threshold the relationship layer is rolled back to the last version that passed. false = never run (also skips generating anchor answers).
persona._comment_evidence: A stable trait becomes a proposal only with at least min_evidence distinct evidence fragments spread over at least min_days different days.
persona._comment_prompt: The <relationship_context> block in the chat prompt (relationship layer + stable traits with confidence >= min_confidence) is capped at max_prompt_lines lines and its own token budget (chars / 4), separate from context.memory_token_budget.
persona._comment_drift: drift_threshold applies to the mean embedding cosine similarity; drift_threshold_jaccard applies when embeddings are unavailable and the check falls back to two-character Jaccard (which reads much lower for paraphrases). drift_samples = answers averaged per probe (temperature is always 0).
persona._comment_judgment: An entity's judgment (the assistant's impression of a person) is updated incrementally: the previous version is the anchor, and a rewrite is kept only if it cites valid source fragments and changes at most this fraction of the text (character-level edit distance / longer length). Otherwise the old version is kept and the rejection is logged.

recall._comment: Retrieval timing gate (G1). gate=false restores the old behaviour exactly (search 8 fragments on every message, random 40% surfacing, unlimited hard triggers, novelty by read_count). Word lists match Simplified and Traditional alike.
recall._comment_verify: CA1 check before replying (off by default). When the message mentions concrete details (dates, weekdays, numbers, times, known people or places) and memories were retrieved, one extra LLM call checks whether the memories support those details. On a mismatch (asked about Friday, memory says Wednesday) or a miss, a <memory_check> note tells the reply model not to use the near-miss memory. Skipped on timeout or error.

emotion._comment: Eight-dimension emotion engine (Plutchik: joy, trust, fear, surprise, sadness, disgust, anger, anticipation). Scribe emits scores for each fact in the same LLM call (no extra calls); the engine learns a personal, time-of-day baseline per dimension (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck + Kalman, hierarchical shrinkage) and flags emotional turning points. enabled=false: Scribe stops emitting emotion fields and nothing else in this section runs.
emotion._comment_timezone: IANA timezone used for time-of-day slots (morning 05-11, noon 11-17, evening 17-23, night 23-05) and weekday.
emotion._comment_noise_floor: Scores at or below this are treated as background noise (measured: neutral short sentences land at 0.1-0.2 on every dimension). Subtracted before intensity/valence.
emotion._comment_learning: Fewer informative fragments than this = still learning (population priors dominate). prior_* = population prior (baseline, spread); tau_hours = recovery time (prior only); obs_noise = Kalman observation noise; shrink_*_n0 = pseudo-observations of the prior.
emotion._comment_fade: Fading affect bias for ranking: negative emotion intensity halves every 60 days, positive every 120. Raw scores are never modified.

scribe._comment_prompt: Extraction prompt. 'v2' (default) = the reorganized prompt (services/hippocampus/entorhinal/scribePromptV2.js): about half the length, one consistent rule (record every concrete detail the user mentions; only the listed exclusions are skipped) instead of the original's conflicting 'fewer but better / when unsure, skip' versus 'never miss anything'. Duplicates are left to the deterministic deduplication. The output format is identical. 'legacy' = the original prompt, unchanged byte for byte. v2 became the default after it answered more questions correctly on the Chinese synthetic sets (69% -> 79% short, 71% -> 78% long) without more invented answers.
scribe._comment_max_output_tokens: Output limit for one extraction batch. The original fixed 4096 truncated most batches: a 60-message batch measured about 5,500-6,100 output tokens at the median and up to 12,000, and a truncated reply used to discard the whole batch. Local models are limited by their context size instead; truncated replies are split in half and retried.
scribe._comment_fix_dates: Before storing, check every 'M月D日（週X）' in a memory against the calendar. Models converting 'next Wednesday' often get the weekday right but the date one to three days off. When they disagree: a date written in the quote wins and the weekday is fixed; otherwise a relative phrase in the quote (下週三, 明天) is recomputed from the message date; otherwise the weekday wins and the date moves to the nearest such weekday.

librarian._comment: Exclude specific fragment sources from search results.
librarian._comment_ranking: Retrieval ranking. 'v2' (default) = the ranking fix measured on LoCoMo and the Chinese synthetic set (eval/results/*_fix/); 'legacy' = the old behaviour exactly (entity channel adds the entity's newest N fragments as candidates, FTS-only results x0.7, a 0.005 floor on the decayed score that drops old memories). Every key below is optional; invalid values fall back to the defaults shown and only apply to v2.
librarian._comment_entity_boost: Candidates already found by FTS/vector that are linked to an entity named in the message get relevance x (1 + entity_boost). The entity no longer injects its own candidates. The user's and the AI's own names never trigger it.
librarian._comment_fts_only_penalty: Relevance multiplier for results found by FTS only (no vector confirmation). The old 0.7 was for single-character CJK indexing; with two-character tokens (W4) it only pushed correct answers down, so the default is 1.0 (no penalty).
librarian._comment_decay_weight: Time decay affects ORDER only, never whether a memory is returned. Rank score = relevance x (decay x recency)^decay_weight x importance x novelty. 0 = time ignored, 1 = old strength. RRF scores are flat, so even small values reorder noticeably.
librarian._comment_min_relevance: Keep/drop threshold on relevance (fused RRF score incl. entity boost; excludes decay/importance/novelty), so very old but relevant memories are still returned. The recall gate's relative cutoff (recall.relative_cutoff) also compares relevance.
librarian._comment_candidate_overfetch: FTS fetches limit x this many candidates so entity boost and time ordering can promote relevant results from just outside the top limit.

tag_routing._comment: 按值標自動建星座：提取時打的標 → 一顆專門的星座（程式碼直連，不靠分類器）。可選值跑 scripts/list_tag_routing.js 看。不填 = 一顆都不建。
tag_routing._example: intimacy -> 親密時刻, health -> 健康

lifecycle._comment: Lifecycle thresholds for the daily maintenance run. Every key is optional and must be a positive integer; invalid values fall back to the defaults shown.
lifecycle._comment_fragment_cooling_days: Active fragments nobody has read/cited for this many days become 'cooling' (1-3650).
lifecycle._comment_fragment_frozen_days: Days a fragment stays cooling before it is frozen and its vector is deleted from ChromaDB (1-3650).
lifecycle._comment_fragment_tombstone_days: Days after freezing before the content is wiped, leaving only the evidence chain (1-3650).
lifecycle._comment_episode_mature_months: Months untouched before an episode matures and its weight is halved (1-120). A month counts as 30 days; flash episodes use twice this.
lifecycle._comment_episode_archive_months: Months before a mature episode is archived (1-120). A month counts as 30 days; flash episodes use twice this.
lifecycle._comment_min_frags_for_entity: Minimum number of fragments an entity needs before it is extracted (1-100).
lifecycle._comment_correction_days_lookback: How many days back the correction-feedback pass looks (1-365).
